chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said concerning an insane woman who committed zina and became pregnant: “She is like one let loose, having no control over her affair; there is neither rajm upon her, nor flogging, nor exile.”

And he said concerning a woman who admitted about herself that a man had forced her against herself: “She is like one let loose, having no control over herself; had he wished, he could have killed her. So there is neither flogging upon her, nor exile, nor rajm.”

key_terms.اسْتَكْرَهَهَا: he forced her against her will
key_terms.السَّائِبَةِ: one left uncontrolled or without command over her own affair in this context
key_terms.مَجْنُونَةٍ: an insane woman lacking legal accountability
key_terms.نَفْيٌ: banishment or exile as a legal penalty

ai.seo_question: Are hadd punishments applied to an insane or coerced woman in cases of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the hadd punishments for zina are not applied to a woman who lacks legal agency, such as an insane woman or a woman coerced into the act. It emphasizes the absence of culpability where control and consent are absent, placing responsibility in accordance with capacity and volition.
